nights.prompt_together: Big light off for the last hour tonight. Lamps only, and whatever conversation the dark end of the evening produces.
nights.prompt_solo: Turn the big light off tonight and put a lamp on instead. Sit in it.
nights.why_line: A room lit for chores and a room lit for company are not the same room.

nights.prompt_together: Eat tonight somewhere that isn’t the usual seat. The floor, the back steps, the room nobody uses.
nights.prompt_solo: Move tonight’s meal somewhere that isn’t the usual seat, and call them over to it.
nights.why_line: Most couples have one chair each and years of the same view.

nights.prompt_together: Give tonight a name before it starts. A quiet one, a silly one, an early one. Then run it that way.
nights.prompt_solo: Decide what kind of evening you want tonight to be, and steer it there without announcing the plan.
nights.why_line: An evening nobody names gets spent on whatever asks loudest.

nights.prompt_together: Fifteen minutes tonight where neither of you is allowed to be useful. Nothing gets tidied, fixed or prepared.
nights.prompt_solo: Take fifteen minutes tonight where you refuse to be useful, in the same room as them.
nights.why_line: Being useful is how two people share a house for a decade and miss each other.

nights.prompt_together: Watch the thing you’ve both been saving. No folding, no second screen, no phones face up.
nights.prompt_solo: Start the thing you’ve both been meaning to watch and leave your phone in another room.
nights.why_line: Half-watching together is just sitting near somebody.

nights.prompt_together: One of you reads aloud for ten minutes. A chapter, an article, the worst reviews of a restaurant you like.
nights.prompt_solo: Read them something out loud tonight because it’s good, not because they need to know it.
nights.why_line: Being read to is the oldest way of being kept company.

nights.prompt_together: Each of you name one thing you’re looking forward to this week. Small is allowed. Small is normal.
nights.prompt_solo: Ask what they’re looking forward to this week, and remember the answer.
nights.why_line: People stop mentioning what they want when nobody asks about it.

nights.prompt_together: Guess out loud how their week has actually been going, before they tell you. Then find out how close you were.
nights.prompt_solo: Say what you think their week has been like and let them correct you.
nights.why_line: A guess is affection with the work shown.

nights.prompt_together: Ask about somebody in their week you never hear about. A coworker, a neighbor, whoever keeps coming up.
nights.prompt_solo: Ask about one of the people in their days you’ve never actually asked about.
nights.why_line: Half of anyone’s life happens among people the other half never meets.

nights.prompt_together: Find out what each of you is in the middle of right now. A book, a project, a slow argument with the insurance company.
nights.prompt_solo: Ask what they’re halfway through at the moment, then ask how they want it to end.
nights.why_line: Everyone is halfway through something, and nobody mentions it unless asked.

nights.prompt_together: Ask what they’ve changed their mind about lately. A person, a plan, a brand of coffee. Anything counts.
nights.prompt_solo: Ask what they’ve stopped liking lately, or come around to.
nights.why_line: People quietly revise themselves and rarely get asked about the edits.

nights.prompt_together: Work out what time tonight each of you finally stops being on duty. Be in the same room when it happens.
nights.prompt_solo: Notice the moment tonight when they stop being on duty, and be nearby for it.
nights.why_line: There is a point in every evening when the day lets go, and theirs is worth knowing.

nights.prompt_together: Plan the trip you’re not taking. Ten minutes, imaginary budget, real arguing about the itinerary.
nights.prompt_solo: Ask where they’d go if a free week appeared out of nowhere, and plan it properly with them.
nights.why_line: Deciding things together is fun long before anything gets booked.

nights.prompt_together: Pass notes on the same sofa for ten minutes. Paper, nonsense only.
nights.prompt_solo: Pass them a pointless note from across the room and see how long it keeps going.
nights.why_line: Couples pass notes at the start, then only grocery lists.

nights.prompt_together: Find the worst photograph of yourself on your phone and show them. See if they can beat it.
nights.prompt_solo: Show them the worst picture of yourself you can find and ask whether they can do worse.
nights.why_line: Being unimpressive on purpose is a kind of trust.

nights.prompt_together: One of you names a year you were both around for. The other says where you lived and what you were like then. Swap.
nights.prompt_solo: Name a year and see what they remember about the two of you in it.
nights.why_line: You have a shared archive and almost never open it.

nights.prompt_together: Two truths and a lie about your week, each. The other has to spot the lie.
nights.prompt_solo: Tell them three things about your week, one of them invented, and see if they catch it.
nights.why_line: You have to listen properly to win, which is the whole trick.

nights.prompt_together: Ask each other three silly questions, and guess each answer before it comes. Make up new ones every time. Points for nothing.
nights.prompt_solo: Guess their answer to something silly before you ask it, then ask.
nights.why_line: Being predicted correctly is oddly flattering. So is being surprising.

nights.prompt_together: Thank each other for one thing so reliable it stopped getting mentioned.
nights.prompt_solo: Say thank you tonight for something they always do and never get told about.
nights.why_line: The dependable things are the first to go invisible.

nights.prompt_together: Two minutes for the small stuff. One sentence each about anything minor from this week, and then it’s closed. Nothing to say is a fine answer.
nights.prompt_solo: Say the small thing you’ve been carrying from this week, once and lightly, then leave it there.
nights.why_line: Most of what curdles between two people was small and easily said at the time.

nights.prompt_together: Ask each other for a favor you’d normally just do yourself.
nights.prompt_solo: Ask them for something small you’d usually handle alone.
nights.why_line: Asking is a quiet compliment. It says you expect a yes.

nights.prompt_together: Two sentences each: one thing that went better than expected this week, one that didn’t. Neither is a problem to solve tonight.
nights.prompt_solo: Tell them how your week actually went, the good half and the other half, and ask for nothing.
nights.why_line: Long-term couples get very good at fixing each other’s weeks and out of practice at hearing them.

nights.prompt_together: Take one thing off the other’s week. Do it, then say it’s handled so they can stop carrying it.
nights.prompt_solo: Quietly take one job off their week, then tell them it’s done.
nights.why_line: Carrying a task is most of the work. The task itself is usually ten minutes.

nights.prompt_together: Say to each other the good thing you’d say about them to somebody else. Out loud, tonight, no occasion.
nights.prompt_solo: The next good thing you catch yourself thinking about them, say it instead of keeping it.
nights.why_line: Most people praise their partner most accurately when their partner is out of the room.
